title: Dietitians and Nutritionists
description: Plan and conduct food service or nutritional programs to assist in the promotion of health and control of disease. May supervise activities of a department providing quantity food services, counsel individuals, or conduct nutritional research.

tasks.text: Evaluate laboratory tests in preparing nutrition recommendations.
Incorporate patient cultural, ethnic, or religious preferences and needs in the development of nutrition plans.
Record and evaluate patient and family health and food history, including symptoms, environmental toxic exposure, allergies, medication factors, and preventive health-care measures.
Monitor food service operations to ensure conformance to nutritional, safety, sanitation and quality standards.
Inspect meals served for conformance to prescribed diets and standards of palatability and appearance.
Coordinate diet counseling services.
Manage quantity food service departments or clinical and community nutrition services.
Organize, develop, analyze, test, and prepare special meals, such as low-fat, low-cholesterol, or chemical-free meals.
Prepare and administer budgets for food, equipment, and supplies.
Coordinate recipe development and standardization and develop new menus for independent food service operations.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Counsel individuals and groups on basic rules of good nutrition, healthy eating habits, and nutrition monitoring to improve their quality of life.
Advise patients and their families on nutritional principles, dietary plans, diet modifications, and food selection and preparation.
Make recommendations regarding public policy, such as nutrition labeling, food fortification, or nutrition standards for school programs.

Advise food service managers and organizations on sanitation, safety procedures, menu development, budgeting, and planning to assist with establishment, operation, and evaluation of food service facilities and nutrition programs.
Develop curriculum and prepare manuals, visual aids, course outlines, and other materials used in teaching.
Write research reports and other publications to document and communicate research findings.
Plan and prepare grant proposals to request program funding.
Develop recipes and menus to address special nutrition needs, such as low glycemic, low histamine, or gluten- or allergen-free.
Develop policies for food service or nutritional programs to assist in health promotion and disease control.
Select, train, and supervise workers who plan, prepare, and serve meals.
Plan and conduct training programs in dietetics, nutrition, and institutional management and administration for medical students, health-care personnel, and the general public.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Consult with physicians and health care personnel to determine nutritional needs and diet restrictions of patient or client.
Confer with design, building, and equipment personnel to plan for construction and remodeling of food service units.
Assess nutritional needs, diet restrictions, and current health plans to develop and implement dietary-care plans and provide nutritional counseling.
Purchase food in accordance with health and safety codes.
Plan, conduct, and evaluate dietary, nutritional, and epidemiological research.
Plan, conduct, and evaluate nutrigenomic or nutrigenetic research.
Test new food products and equipment.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Allergenic diet software, Aurora FoodPro, Axxya Systems Nutritionist Pro, Compu-Cal Nutrition Assistant.
